title: Thunder's Edge expedition in the turn bar
description: Why a tester never saw the Thunder's Edge options, and what a table with the content switched on now offers. Every game shot is a real offline game: the rules engine in a Web Worker, rule bots, seed 12, 3 players, and (where the caption says so) the dev start preset `expedition`, which has the bots hold four of the six slices so the human can finish the expedition in round 1. The expedition is committed at the end of a player's turn (the closing menu), uses no action, and one slice can be claimed per turn.

shots.caption: New row 'Thunder's Edge content', off by default. Off plays the Prophecy of Kings content, which is what every game played before the switch.

shots.caption: Ticked: the game is played with every source, which brings in the expedition and the faction breakthroughs it grants.

shots.heading: What the tester saw: switch off (390x844)
shots.caption: A new offline game before this change: the Components button reads 'Nothing usable now' and no Thunder's Edge option exists, because the engine played the Prophecy of Kings sources, which do not contain Thunder's Edge.

shots.heading: Switch on, before the action (390x844)
shots.caption: Components now has a Thunder's Edge group. Before the turn's action every slice waits: the expedition is committed at the end of the turn. Claimed slices name the bot that holds them; the group says how many are taken, how many you hold, and which breakthrough your first claim grants.

shots.caption: The same on desktop.

shots.caption: After the action the turn is closing: Components says '2 usable' next to End turn.

shots.heading: Slices and who holds them (390x844)
shots.caption: The two slices the seat can pay come first (discard a secret objective, exhaust a technology-specialty planet); the four taken ones say 'Claimed by Bot 2 / Bot 3'.

shots.heading: Slices and who holds them (desktop)
shots.caption: The same on desktop.

shots.heading: Hover: the breakthrough (desktop)
shots.caption: The side panel names the card the first claim grants (Bellum Gloriosum, synergy Biotic + Cybernetic) with its printed text.

shots.heading: One slice per turn (390x844)
shots.caption: After a slice is claimed (the only secret objective is discarded without asking) the other open slice is not offered again this turn.

shots.heading: One slice per turn (desktop)
shots.caption: The same on desktop.

shots.heading: The last slice (390x844)
shots.caption: Second turn of the same game: five slices are taken, the sixth (exhaust a technology-specialty planet) is the one that completes the expedition.

shots.heading: Choose the system (390x844)
shots.caption: The finisher places Thunder's Edge. The printed rule wants a system with no planet, supernova or printed wormhole; generated maps have none (their filler is planet systems only), so a table with the content on falls back to neutral systems and the prompt says so. 'Choose on the map' works as for any system pick.

shots.heading: Choose the system (desktop)
shots.caption: The same on desktop.

shots.heading: Tie: who places the infantry (390x844)
shots.caption: Three seats hold two slices each; the finisher chooses which of them places the infantry (a rules tie-break).

shots.heading: Tie: who places the infantry (desktop)
shots.caption: The same on desktop.

shots.heading: Thunder's Edge on the map (desktop)
shots.caption: The planet stands in the chosen system (second chip on tile #21), the seat that claimed the first slice holds its breakthrough (Bellum Gloriosum, unlocked in the player sheet), the secret objective is gone, and the expedition group has left Components.

shots.heading: Thunder's Edge placed (390x844)
shots.caption: The same on a phone: Components is back to 'Nothing usable now'.

shots.heading: The system inspector (desktop)
shots.caption: Thunder's Edge: 5 resources, 1 influence, legendary (Jupiter Brain), controlled by the placer with 2 infantry on it. A planet placed during the game used to show its id and 0/0 here; it now takes its name and values from the catalog.

shots.heading: The system inspector (390x844)
shots.caption: The same on a phone.

notes.title: Reproduce
notes.text: cd web && npm run build:wasm && rm -rf node_modules/.vite && npm run screenshots -- FP (needs cargo with the wasm32-unknown-unknown target; TI4_WASM_FILE=<file> reuses a prebuilt engine).

notes.title: Why the start preset
notes.text: Reaching the sixth slice by play takes many rounds and the dumb click driver of the offline captures does not get through them. The dev-only 'Start preset' field of the offline form (dev builds only) starts the engine's `expedition` preset: Thunder's Edge on, four slices claimed by the bots (with their breakthroughs), and the first seat holding a secret objective and a technology-specialty planet. Everything after that is the real engine and the real UI.

notes.title: Not shown
notes.text: The discard prompts of the action-card and trade-good slices and the choice of which specialty planet pays are covered by engine and host tests (a seat holding exactly one candidate is not asked). Choosing a planet pays through the same planet picker as any planet pick.
